obtaining the records & the dataset's two streams, covering all 31 December days. One stream records each modification to the visible book, with the order's identifier, side, price and new size but no timestamp; the other records every order event, timestamped to the nanosecond & each archive verified against its expected MD5 checksum after download \\
timestamping the book changes & each book change receives the nanosecond timestamp of its order event, matched on the order's identifier & matches that invert at sub-second resolution are resolved by the phantom-order rule below \\
warming up the replay & the first 1,500,000 changes are applied without being recorded. The replay starts from an empty book, and learns of an order only when that order changes, so it holds too little volume until the orders present at the start have gone & recording begins 12.5 minutes into 1 December, leaving hour 0 of that day short of book data and outside the regime split, the only such hour of the month's 744 \\
removing phantom orders & 4,345 orders across the month are removed before they appear. In the sub-second ordering of the two streams, a cancellation can be recorded before the order it cancels & one rule, applied uniformly across the month. Without it, such orders rest in the book indefinitely \\
building the half-second book & the book rebuilt at twenty levels per side and sampled at half-second intervals, giving 5,355,301 book states over the month & the reconstruction is verified by the independent pass in the final row \\
labelling and splitting the hours & each of 743 hours labelled calm or volatile at the \$3.53 median threshold on one-second price volatility, which separates a median calm hour of \$2.37 from a median volatile hour of \$5.44; 557 earlier hours eligible for fitting, the later 186 reserved for testing & within each group, every fitting hour predates all of its held-back hours \\
verifying the reconstruction & a second, independent pass over the same raw records, advancing the book event by event, and sampling it back to the same half-second points & the two methods agree exactly, across all 5,355,301 states \\
